To: Renters Board / Notices
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT FOR REVIEW — stop using Brightline Pro 6%, batch LX2291

DRAFT — not for posting until I’ve checked it.

Everyone, please check your developer before your next colour. Kelvin Trade has confirmed a filling error with Brightline Pro 6% (20 vol) Cream Developer 1L. Batch LX2291 may actually contain 12% (40 vol). That’s double the labelled strength, not just a slightly stronger mix.

STOP USING BATCH LX2291 NOW

The affected batch was supplied between 19 October and 5 November 2026. Check every bottle, including open ones in your trolley and stock in the back. Don’t assume an opened bottle is fine because you’ve already used it.

The batch code is on the BASE OF THE BOTTLE, not the box. Please turn each bottle over and check it properly. If you can’t read the code, put that bottle aside and get Kelvin Trade to confirm it before using it.

Keep affected bottles separate from usable stock and clearly mark them “DO NOT USE”. Don’t try to dilute them, adjust your mixing ratio or use them for a different service. Kelvin Trade says other batches and other strengths are not affected.

WHAT’S HAPPENED HERE

On Saturday, I used a new bottle from batch LX2291 for a bleach retouch. The lift was much faster than expected, and the client developed burning and red areas on the scalp. I stopped and rinsed immediately. No client details are being shared here.

Another renter has also reported unusually fast lift and very hot foils with this same batch. Please don’t put unexpected heat down to the heater or assume tingling is normal if it continues or gets worse.

WHAT IT CAN DO

Developer that is stronger than the label says can make bleach or colour behave differently from what you’re expecting. You may see very rapid lift, excessive heat, uneven results, dryness, weakened hair or breakage. It can also irritate or chemically burn the scalp. Faster lift is not a good result if the hair or skin is being damaged.

A patch test does not check whether a bottle contains the correct developer strength. It is not a reason to carry on using this batch.

IF SOMEONE REACTS IN THE CHAIR

Stop the service straight away. Don’t wait for the timer, blistering or severe pain.

For a suspected chemical burn, follow the salon’s first-aid guidance:
• Call 999 for medical help immediately.
• Protect yourself with gloves. Carefully remove contaminated clothing if possible.
• Rinse the affected area with plenty of cool or lukewarm running water for about one hour. Follow the call handler’s instructions.
• Don’t use shampoo, creams, aloe, neutralisers or other chemicals on the affected area.
• Chemical burns need hospital assessment. Breathing difficulty, throat swelling or collapse also require 999 immediately.

Once urgent care is underway, record what happened in the incident book at the desk. Keep factual notes of the products, batch, mixing ratio, timings, symptoms and action taken. Keep client details and any photographs private, not on this board.

RETURNS — AND KEEPING EVIDENCE

The Kelvin Trade rep is in on Tuesday, 10 November. Affected bottles can go back to him or to the Hillington depot for a full credit.

If you’ve had a problem, KEEP THE BOTTLE involved, including any remaining product. Don’t bin it or hand that particular bottle back before checking with your insurer about retaining evidence. Keep the supplier email, purchase details and dated incident records too.

Please flag this to anyone else in the building who buys from the same rep. Check the bottle base, check the trolley, check the back stock. This needs caught before another client gets hurt.

Kirsty
